text: This video writes the actual handoff document for the Wrenfield knowledge assistant -- what it does, what it doesn't, and who owns each piece.
It states real capabilities plainly: grounded, cited answers across HR, IT, and Ops documents, and a real 'I don't know' when the documents don't support an answer.
It documents the security incident as a named lesson learned -- ingesting every file with no status filter is exactly what let a stale draft carry a hidden instruction into production.
Ownership is stated by name: Jordan Vance owns the assistant, Caleb Shaw owns deployment, and Lena Ortiz owns ongoing security review.
And it states honestly how someone would know this needs attention today -- a failed red-team eval, or an unusual response flagged for human review.
